names.official: State income tax on earned and capital income (with the broadcasting tax)

taxes.base: Earned income (wages, pensions, benefits, business income) and capital income (interest, dividends, rents, capital gains) of individuals.
taxes.payer: Individuals; employers and payers withhold it from wages and pensions.

rate.headline: Progressive on earned income; flat on capital income
details: Earned income is taxed on a progressive scale with several brackets; the State levy comes on top of the municipal tax.
Capital income has its own rates, with a higher rate above a threshold.
The line also includes the public broadcasting tax (2.5% of income above EUR 15,150, at most EUR 160), which the source does not itemise.

instruments.explanation: The Tax Administration reports that withholding on wages, pensions and taxable benefits brought in EUR 36.8 billion in 2025, shared between the State, the municipalities and the church; the line drawn is the State’s part.

taxes.base: Profits of companies and other corporate entities resident in Finland and Finnish-source profits of others.

details: The revenue is shared by a fixed formula between the State, municipalities and parishes.

instruments.explanation: Fell slightly in 2025 (by EUR 60 million), after larger falls in the two previous years.

taxes.base: Interest paid on deposits and bonds to individuals.
taxes.payer: The bank deducts it from the interest.

instruments.explanation: The final tax on interest paid to individuals, in place of a return.

taxes.base: Inheritances and gifts received, by the relationship between giver and receiver.
taxes.payer: The person who receives the inheritance or gift.

rate.headline: Progressive, by relationship
details: Close relatives are taxed at lower rates than others; the rates are in the Act.

instruments.explanation: The only wealth-transfer tax; it raised about EUR 1.1 billion in 2025.

taxes.base: The price paid when real estate, shares in housing companies and other securities change hands.

rate.headline: 3% on real estate; 1.5% on shares and securities
details: First-time home buyers aged 18 to 39 are exempt for their first home.

instruments.explanation: Revenue follows turnover in the housing and share markets.

taxes.base: Supplies of goods and services in Finland and imports, with credit for tax on business purchases.
taxes.payer: Consumers; businesses charge it and remit the balance.

rate.headline: 25.5% standard; 14%, 10% reduced
details: The standard rate rose from 24% to 25.5% on 1 September 2024.
The 14% rate of 2025 (food, restaurants, pharmaceuticals, passenger transport, accommodation) became 13.5% on 1 January 2026; 10% applies to newspapers and magazines.

instruments.explanation: The largest single tax: 23% of the national total. Revenue rose by almost 5% in 2025 mainly because of the higher rate.

names.official: Excise duty on electricity and certain fuels (energy taxes)

taxes.base: Motor fuels, heating fuels, electricity and coal, by quantity, with a carbon element and an energy element.
taxes.payer: Fuel and electricity suppliers; passed on in the price.

rate.headline: Per litre, kilowatt-hour or tonne
details: The rates are in the Act and are adjusted by law.

instruments.explanation: Includes the tax on petrol and diesel, which is the largest part, and the electricity tax.

taxes.base: Alcoholic beverages, by volume of alcohol or of product.
taxes.payer: Producers and importers; passed on in the price.

rate.headline: Per litre of alcohol or product

instruments.explanation: One of the higher alcohol taxes in the EU.

taxes.payer: Manufacturers and importers; passed on in the price.

rate.headline: A specific amount plus a share of the price

instruments.explanation: A tax on cigarettes, cigars, smoking tobacco and similar products.

taxes.payer: Insurers, passed on in the premium.

instruments.explanation: Charged on non-life insurance such as motor, home and property policies.

taxes.base: Ownership of a vehicle: a basic tax by CO2 emissions and an operating tax on diesel and some other fuels.

rate.headline: A daily amount by CO2 band, plus an operating tax

instruments.explanation: Collected by Traficom, the transport agency, not by the Tax Administration.

taxes.base: Cars and motorcycles on first registration in Finland.
taxes.payer: The person who registers the vehicle.

rate.headline: A percentage of the taxable value, by CO2 band

instruments.explanation: A one-off tax at registration, separate from the annual vehicle tax.

taxes.base: Soft drinks, juices and waters with added sugar, by litre.
taxes.payer: Producers and importers; passed on in the price.

instruments.explanation: A small excise on sweetened drinks.

taxes.base: The proceeds of lotteries and gambling.

instruments.explanation: A small tax; the profits of the state gaming company are a separate revenue and are not counted.

names.official: Other small taxes and charges (pharmacy fee, stockpiling fee, mining mineral tax and others)

taxes.base: The pharmacy fee, the emergency stockpiling fee, the mining mineral tax, vehicle registration fees, deposit guarantee fees, fire protection fee, drink packaging excise, game and fishing management fees, the nuclear research fee, the environmental damage fee and the waste tax.
taxes.payer: Pharmacies, importers of fuel, mining companies, banks, drivers, hunters and others.

rate.headline: Each has its own Act
details: Each of these is below 0.2% of the national total; together they are 0.35%.

instruments.explanation: Statistics Finland counts these tax-like payments as taxes on production. Grouped here because none is large enough for a core of its own.

taxes.base: Earned income of individuals (wages, pensions, benefits and business income), after deductions.
taxes.payer: Individuals; withheld with the State income tax.

rate.headline: A flat rate set by each municipality: 4.7%–10.9% in 2025
details: The average rate was 7.54% in 2025 (Ministry of Finance). The church tax of 1.00%–2.25% is a separate levy of the churches and is not drawn.

instruments.explanation: The main tax of local government. The rates are lower than before 2023, when health and social care moved to the wellbeing services counties.

taxes.base: The taxable value of land and buildings, set by the Tax Administration.

rate.headline: A rate set by each municipality within legal bands
details: The general rate is 0.41% to 2.00% depending on the type; vacant plots in a town plan area can be taxed at 2% to 6%.

instruments.explanation: The second tax of local government, after the municipal income tax.

taxes.base: Wages and income from self-employment of everyone working in Finland.
taxes.payer: Employers and employees (the self-employed pay in full).

rate.headline: A share of earnings, set each year
details: Employers and employees pay separate shares of earnings; the source gives the amounts only, not the rates.

instruments.explanation: The statutory pension scheme is run by private pension insurers and funds, but the contributions are fixed by law and counted as social security. Employers pay EUR 19.0 billion and employees EUR 9.2 billion.

taxes.base: Earnings, for the health insurance contribution, the unemployment insurance premium and the other statutory schemes.

rate.headline: By scheme
details: The employee’s health insurance contribution was 1.06% of earned income in 2025.

instruments.explanation: Employers paid EUR 2.6 billion and the insured EUR 3.1 billion. The source does not split the line by scheme.
